CHOICE: 3

Solution 1 correctly applies the stars and bars method and correctly calculates the number of ways as 3. Solution 2 makes a valid point about the possible distributions but miscounts by one, considering only the symmetrical cases as distinct. Solution 3 also correctly identifies the number of distinct distributions but incorrectly counts as there are 6, not 4. The correct number of ways to distribute 5 indistinguishable balls into 2 indistinguishable boxes is indeed 3, as each arrangement can be seen as a distinct partition of the total number of balls into two groups.
